title: Umag Prices and Realistic 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Umag costs in 2027: daily budgets, apartment and hotel rates, food, beach, transport and tourist tax, plus how prices have shifted since the euro switch.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Umag Cost in 2027?

Umag sits at the northwest tip of Istria, about 15 km from the Slovenian border and roughly 30 km from the Piran area. It is cheaper than Dubrovnik, Split or Hvar, but it is no longer a bargain. Prices rose after Croatia adopted the euro in 2023, and Istria has stayed one of the busiest and most expensive regions on the Croatian coast.

The figures below are based on 2026 price levels plus an expected rise of about 3–5% for 2027. Treat them as planning ranges, not fixed quotes.

## How Prices in Umag Have Changed Recently

- **Accommodation:** Rates in Umag have kept rising by a few percent a year. Peak-season apartments now commonly start around €90 per night and reach €180 for larger units near the sea.
- **Demand:** Istria reported fiscalised turnover up around 15% in early summer 2026. Visitors are comparing prices more closely, but bookings have not dropped.
- **Public debate:** The price debate in Croatia has been loud since euro adoption. Tourists in Istria are split on whether Croatia now costs more than Spain or Greece.
- **Tourist tax:** Umag charges €1.60 per person per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.10 for the rest of the year (2026 rates). The Istria County Assembly adopted a separate 2027 tax decision in November 2025, so check the final 2027 figure when booking. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12–17 pay half.

## Daily Budget by Travel Style (Per Person)

| Style | Per person per day | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €60–€80 | Shared apartment or campsite, groceries, one cheap meal out, bike or walking |
| Mid-range | €100–€160 | 3-star hotel or private apartment, two restaurant meals, a paid activity |
| Luxury | €220+ | 4–5-star resort, fine dining, boat trips, spa |

A couple traveling mid-range in peak season should plan €200–€350 per day all in. In May, June or September the same trip falls to roughly €150–€250.

## Accommodation Costs in Umag

### Apartments and Studios
The largest group of lodging. Expect €60–€120 per night in shoulder months and €90–€180 in July and August. Many sit within 1–2 km of the sea. Properties in the old town and near the promenade cost more than those near the edge of Umag. A week in peak season for two typically comes to €630–€1,260.

### Hotels
Three-star hotels average roughly €70–€100 per night, with peak dates higher. Four-star properties run about €130–€280. The Plava Laguna group runs several large hotels and residences on the Punta peninsula, including Hotel Umag, Hotel Aurora, Hotel Pelegrin and Garden Suites. Hotels in Stella Maris and the Sol Garden Istra complex sit on the Katoro and Stella Maris side of town and suit families who want pools and kids' clubs. The Hotel Umag has a guest rating of around 8.2/10.

### Campsites
Camping Park Umag at Ladin Gaj is the budget route. Campsites charge the same €1.60 tourist tax as hotels in season, and pitch prices rise sharply in July and August.

### Inland Stays
Agriturismos and rural villas near Momjan, Grožnjan and Buje usually charge €90–€180 for a double room. They need a car, but they often include breakfast and local wine.

## Food and Drink Prices

- **Coffee:** about €2–€2.50 for an espresso or macchiato on the main squares.
- **Beer (0.3–0.5 l):** about €3.50–€5.
- **Konoba main course:** €15–€25 for pasta, grilled fish or meat; fresh fish is sold by weight and is the item most likely to surprise a bill.
- **Mid-range dinner for two:** about €50–€90 with wine, and up to €100 at better places.
- **Fast food or bakery lunch:** €5–€10.
- **Local wine tasting:** about €25 per person at wineries such as Kabola, around 15 km from Umag.

Groceries from Konzum, Studenac or Lidl cut daily costs substantially. A self-catering couple can eat well on €30–€45 a day.

**Opinion:** The waterfront terraces on the main promenade are usually not worth the premium. Walking five to ten minutes into the side streets, or driving to a konoba such as Buščina outside the center, gives better food at lower prices.

## Getting Around and Activities

- **Bike rental:** about €20–€30 per day. The coastal path toward Savudrija and the lighthouse is flat and easy.
- **Car:** Umag is about 85 km from Pula Airport and 70 km from Trieste Airport. Rentals in peak season often cost €50–€90 per day. Parking in town is paid in summer zones.
- **Truffle hunting tours** in the Motovun area: about €80–€120 per person, around a 45-minute drive away.
- **Beaches:** Most Umag beaches are pebble or rock with concrete platforms. Public access is free, but sunbed rental on the main beaches adds roughly €10–€20 per set per day.
- **Tennis:** Umag hosts the Croatia Open ATP tournament each July, and hotel prices rise during it.

## Peak vs Shoulder Season Comparison

July and August have the highest prices, the most traffic, and the most crowded beaches. May, June and September offer sea temperatures that are fine for swimming from mid-June to late September and noticeably lower rates. October and November bring lower prices still, but many seasonal restaurants and beach services close.

## Local Tips for Saving Money

1. **Book in the first quarter.** Good apartments close to the sea fill by April for July and August.
2. **Pick weekdays.** Many hosts charge more for Saturday-to-Saturday stays in high season.
3. **Choose inland for value.** Agriturismo rooms 15–20 km inland come with parking and cheaper dining.
4. **Check the tax.** Hotels often add tourist tax at the end. Budget about €11 per person for a week in season.
5. **Use the Slovenian border.** Fuel and some groceries can differ in price, so compare before filling up.

## Is Umag Expensive Compared With Other Croatian Destinations?

Umag is moderate. It costs less than Dubrovnik and Split and is close to Poreč and Novigrad. Rovinj is generally the most expensive of the Istrian coastal towns. Umag is a sensible choice for families and travelers who want a calm town with good bike paths, a working old center and quick access to Slovenia and Italy.

## Sample 7-Night Budget for Two in 2027

| Category | Mid-range, shoulder | Mid-range, peak |
|---|---|---|
| Accommodation | €560–€840 | €750–€1,260 |
| Food and drink | €350–€500 | €450–€650 |
| Activities and transport | €100–€200 | €150–€300 |
| Tourist tax | €22 | €22 |
| **Total** | **€1,030–€1,560** | **€1,370–€2,230** |

Add airfare or fuel and tolls from your origin on top of this.

faq.question: How much does a week in Umag cost in 2027?
faq.answer: A couple should plan roughly €1,000–€1,600 for a mid-range week in shoulder season and €1,400–€2,250 in July or August, excluding travel to Croatia. Budget travelers who self-cater can bring this down to about €700–€1,000.

faq.question: Is Umag expensive?
faq.answer: Umag is moderately priced. It is cheaper than Dubrovnik and Split, but prices in peak season are well above the Croatian average, and costs have risen each year since the euro switch.

faq.question: How much is the tourist tax in Umag?
faq.answer: In 2026 the tax was €1.60 per person per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.10 the rest of the year. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12–17 pay half. A separate decision covers 2027, so confirm with your host.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Umag?
faq.answer: Late September and October, and May to early June, give the best mix of lower prices and decent weather. Peak weeks around the July tennis tournament and mid-August are the most expensive.

faq.question: How much does a restaurant meal cost in Umag?
faq.answer: A main course at a konoba usually costs €15–€25, and a dinner for two with wine is about €50–€90. Fresh fish by weight can push the bill higher.

faq.question: What is the average hotel price in Umag?
faq.answer: Three-star hotels average roughly €70–€100 per night and four-star hotels about €130–€280 in season. Private apartments from €60 in shoulder season are usually the better value.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Umag?
faq.answer: Not for a stay in town, since the old center, promenade and beaches are walkable or reachable by bike. A car is useful for inland Istria, wineries and truffle tours, and for airport transfers from Pula or Trieste.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 budget for Umag is about €60–€80 per person per day for budget travelers, €100–€160 for mid-range, and €220+ for luxury. A couple in July or August should plan €200–€350 per day. Shoulder months (May, June, September) cut accommodation by roughly 30–40%.
